final_candidates.decision_summary: Gly-to-Pro in the structured Gly19-Gly22 region imposes a rigid backbone kink and blocks backbone H-bonding, strongly destabilizing the small PsaE fold. Verified WT residue G at position 19.
Replacing the likely buried hydrophobic Ile33 with charged Asp is a classic folding-disruptive core mutation. Verified WT residue I at position 33.
Pro at Gly22, adjacent to Gly19, similarly kinks the backbone and disrupts local secondary structure. Verified WT residue G at position 22.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 fold-disrupting mutations are stable across self-review; no external evidence is available to refine further.

history.rationale: Introducing a proline into the conserved YWYGD motif's glycine likely breaks the local backbone conformation required for the thioredoxin-like fold of PsaE.
Gly-to-Pro in a loop/helix region imposes rigid kinks and breaks backbone H-bonding, strongly disrupting the small PsaE fold.
Replacing a core buried hydrophobe in the IYPVI cluster with a charged Asp should severely destabilize the hydrophobic core.
Buried hydrophobic Ile replaced by charged Asp is a classic folding-disruptive core mutation.
The conserved proline in the IIYP loop stabilizes the turn; substitution with glycine increases flexibility and entropic cost of folding.
Pro35 is likely a core or turn-anchoring residue; removing its rigid constraint can collapse local packing, but effect is less certain than charge-in-core mutations.
Glycine in the GDVGT turn region replaced by proline disrupts the required backbone geometry.
Gly22 sits adjacent to Gly19; a Pro here is also highly destabilizing and may be structurally equivalent, so I promote it above P35G.
Phe60 is part of the C-terminal hydrophobic cluster; a charged substitution undermines packing and helix integrity.
Hydrophobic-to-charged substitution in the C-terminal helix region disrupts packing.
Core leucine to aspartate introduces an unfavorable buried charge, destabilizing the first beta-strand/core.
Charged residue in a hydrophobic N-terminal helix position destabilizes the fold.
Buried hydrophobic Ile in the VIVR segment replaced by glutamate disrupts strand packing.
Core Ile-to-Glu is destabilizing but Glu is slightly more tolerable than Asp in buried sites.
Trp17 in the conserved SYWYGD motif is a key structural anchor; alanine substitution removes aromatic packing and motif integrity.
Trp-to-Ala removes a large hydrophobe but Ala remains fold-compatible; weaker knockout than charge-in-core or Pro-in-helix options.

rejection.reason: Trp-to-Ala removes a large hydrophobe but Ala remains fold-compatible; weaker knockout than charge-in-core or Pro-in-helix options.

history.rationale: Glycine within the GSGAGG linker region replaced by proline likely breaks loop geometry connecting structural elements.
Gly53 is in a flexible Gly-rich segment where Pro may be tolerated without global unfolding.

rejection.reason: Gly53 is in a flexible Gly-rich segment where Pro may be tolerated without global unfolding.

history.rationale: Conserved Phe48 in the GFSGS motif to aspartate introduces a buried charge, destabilizing local fold.
Position may be surface-exposed near the partner-binding face; charged substitution is less reliably fold-disruptive than core-targeted options.
